formula: n ~ nL1 + nL2 + w + wL1 + k + kL1 + kL2 + ys + ysL1 + ysL2 + yr1980 + yr1981 + yr1982 + yr1983 + yr1984 + year + (1 | id)
notes: Arellano & Bond (1991) UK firm employment panel, id the firm with yearly rows. The Stata [XT] xtabond example, recalled from the manual: n (log employment) on two lags of n, w and its lag, k and ys with two lags each, yr1980-yr1984 and year, by difference GMM with no random effect. The random intercept per firm is the reader's proposal on those regressors. n, w, k and ys are the logs of emp, wage, cap and indoutpt, which are ignored with the derived year dummies and yearm1. ind (industry) is a possible superior factor of id, left unused. RULE GAP: a random intercept beside a lagged response carries the dynamic-panel bias the documented GMM fit avoids.

Penn World Table real exchange rates, a balanced country-by-year panel; id is labeled Group (country) and duplicates country. The Stata [XT] xtunitroot example tests lnrxrate (log of realxrate) for panel unit roots and fits no regression, so the random intercept per country with a year trend and the OECD and G7 indicators is the reader's proposal. xrate and ppp build realxrate, ignored with them, as the response is its stored log lnrxrate, the column the example tests; capt is unlabeled and ignored. Hand check #120: the response is the stored lnrxrate, not log(realxrate).

Dahlberg & Johansson (2000) Swedish municipality fiscal panel, 1979-1987, idcode the municipality with yearly rows, all three series deflated per capita. The Stata example models the expenditures-revenues-grants dynamics by panel VAR or dynamic GMM on lags, with no random effect; the random intercept per municipality on the contemporaneous series is the reader's proposal. year loads as a datetime and is ignored.

Zuur, Hilbe and Ieno's deep-sea fish example (Bailey et al. 2008). That the book fits a negative binomial GLM of TotAbund on MeanDepth and Period with offset(log(SweptArea)) and no random effect is unverified: its model scripts are password protected, and the original paper (Bailey et al. 2009, Proc. R. Soc. B, PMC2677247) fits a different GAMM. Each Site is one trawl, and every survey Year holds several, so the year random intercept is the reader's proposal; Period is constant within Year. Dens is TotAbund over SweptArea; Xkm and Ykm are coordinates. Hand check #120: the book's model attribution marked unverified.

formula: Surv(t0 - ave(t0, id, FUN = min), t1 - ave(t0, id, FUN = min), failed) ~ pk_dum + victory + treaty + wartype + logdead + faction + polityle + infst + past_ag + garm + contraband + lmtnest + p5_contig1 + p5_col + (1|cluster)
notes: The codebook (figs/pk_pkept_codebook.pdf) documents the file; ROS's peace.R reads pk&pkept_old.dta directly, plots the time to renewed war and fits no model. Rows are time-varying spells (t0, t1] of each ceasefire id, failed marks the spell in which peace fails, and ceasefires repeat within conflicts (cluster: conflict cluster) and countries (clust2: country cluster, ignored as the coarser alternative). The codebook's stset takes each id's earliest t0, the ceasefire date, as the time origin (origin(time t0)), so the formula counts the spells from there. The covariates are those whose Schoenfeld residuals pk&pkept_old.dta carries, so the deposit fitted a Cox model on them; the conflict random intercept is the reader's proposal. RULE GAP: a counting-process Cox response on start-stop spells, which brms's cox family takes no form of. Hand check #120: the spells counted from each ceasefire, not in calendar time.

formula: partyid7 ~ real_ideo + race_adj + factor(age_discrete) + educ1 + female + income + factor(year) + (1 | state)
notes: The rpackage rendering of the NES file, as NES/data/nes_setup.R prepares it. ROS's NES example (nes_linear.R) fits a linear regression of the 7-point partyid7 on real_ideo, race_adj, factor(age_discrete), educ1, female and income separately within each year. The survey wave stays fixed as factor(year); respondents repeat within the 48 states, whose random intercept is the reader's proposal. race and age are the sources of race_adj and age_discrete, year_new recodes year, cd nests in state. Alex's spot check of 2026-10-08 read the wave as fixed and missed the state; an independent judge (2026-10-24) found the state grouping and kept the wave fixed.

ARM Ch.10 regression discontinuity (10.4_LackOfOverlapWhenTreat.AssignmentIsUnknown.R) fits lm(score1 ~ party + x) with party = dvp < 0.5 and x = 1 - dvp on the 1994 incumbents only, the subsets ideo_two_pred, ideo_interactions and ideo_reparam; no multilevel model. The full table repeats each numbered House seat (stgj:cd) over the congresses and holds every seat of a congress under one year, so seat and congress year are rendered as crossed random intercepts, the reader's proposal; that a numbered seat stays one geographic district across redistricting is unproven; party enters as its expression of dvp. congno duplicates year, sticpsr, stalpha and nstate duplicate the state code stgj, score2 is the second ideology score, and dvfix, dvpfix and normvote are the script's incumbency corrections. Hand check #120: stgj:cd read as numbered seats.

formula: cases ~ factor(age) + offset(log(pyr)) + cohort effects by year under a second-order random walk, beta[k] ~ Normal(2 * beta[k-1] - beta[k-2], sigma), Poisson; no exact lme4 representation
documented_prior: sigma ~ uniform(0, 1); beta[1:2] ~ normal(0, sigma * 1E3); beta[k] ~ normal(2 * beta[k - 1] - beta[k - 2], sigma) for k >= 3; alpha ~ normal(0, 1000)
notes: RULE GAP: ice.stan (BUGS Vol2 Ice, non-parametric smoothing in an age-cohort model) fits cases ~ poisson_log(alpha[age] + log(pyr) + beta[year]) with alpha for the first age band fixed at alpha1 = 0 and the cohort effects beta under a second-order random-walk prior of estimated scale sigma; the random walk has no lme4 form, so the formula states the model in words; an exchangeable cohort intercept (1 | year) would alter it. Each birth cohort (year) holds several age bands and each age band several cohorts; age is a fixed categorical effect and pyr (person-years) the offset. pineapple_ice and vanilla_ice hold the same data. Hand check #120: the formula in words, as no lme4 formula holds the model.

formula: dl_gdp ~ hierarchical VAR(2): lags 1 and 2 of dl_gdp, dl_cons and dl_gfcf within country ordered by year; country-specific intercepts and lag coefficients drawn around global means; trivariate normal errors shared with dl_cons and dl_gfcf; random effects by country
documented_prior: rho ~ Beta(2, 2); alpha_hat_location ~ Normal(0, 0.1); alpha_hat_scale ~ InverseGamma(3, 0.5); beta_hat_location ~ Normal(0, 0.1); beta_hat_scale ~ InverseGamma(3, 0.5); omega_global ~ LKJCholeskyCov(eta=1, sd_dist=Exponential(1)); per country z_scale_alpha, z_scale_beta ~ InverseGamma(3, 0.5), alpha ~ Normal(alpha_hat_location, alpha_hat_scale * z_scale_alpha), lag_coefs ~ Normal(beta_hat_location, beta_hat_scale * z_scale_beta), noise_chol ~ LKJCholeskyCov(eta=10, sd_dist=Exponential(1))
notes: RULE GAP: a linear hierarchical VAR with pooled residual Cholesky factors, which no lme4 formula encodes exactly. examples/time_series/bayesian_var_model.myst.md fits make_hierarchical_model(2, 3, df_final, 'country'), a vector autoregression of order 2 over dl_gdp, dl_cons and dl_gfcf, each country's intercepts and lag coefficients drawn independently around global means and its error covariance rho * omega_global + (1 - rho) * noise_chol. Each series enters at its within-country lags 1 and 2, so the GDP equation has six varying lag coefficients, conditionally uncorrelated by country. covariates and random_slopes name the other two series by their columns; dl_gdp's own lags, which no covariate can name, and the lags themselves, which are no columns of the table, are in the formula's words. One row per response; the first reading's exclusion (observations not exchangeable within a country) is no reason against the country grouping. GDP, CONS and GFCF are the levels the dl_ log differences are taken from; year and time order the series. Hand check #120: linear rather than nonlinear, with the other two series as covariates.

formula: I(value * 1000) ~ area-specific piecewise-linear curve over the age midpoint (age_start + age_end) / 2 through ten knots, the knot values a Gaussian random walk per area with one shared step sd; random curves by area
documented_prior: coeff_sd ~ HalfCauchy(5); y ~ GaussianRandomWalk(sigma=coeff_sd, shape=(nknots, ncountries)); sd ~ HalfCauchy(5)
notes: RULE GAP: a per-group random-walk curve has no lme4 form. examples/time_series/GHME_2013.py fits, on the areas CYP, DNK, ESP, FIN, GBR and ISL only, value * 1000 ~ Normal(p, sd) with p interpolated from a per-area Gaussian random walk over ten age knots, no other term; age_start and age_end are its inputs. Rows repeat within each area over ages, years and sexes, so area is a grouping factor although the spot check (Alex 2026-10-07) filed the table for its model having no hierarchical term; the per-area curves share their step scale and the residual sd, and are linear in their knot values, so the model is no nonlinear one. The script's six-area subset is kept in words here. lower_ci, upper_ci, standard_error and effective_sample_size describe value's uncertainty and are unused. Hand check #120: the formula takes the response on the script's per-1,000 scale.

Flat second reading: Fox (2016) uses the table for a simple regression of vocabulary on education; year is the GSS survey year, each wave holding many respondents, so it is filed as the grouping factor, and sex and the random intercept are the reader's proposal. vocabulary is the number correct on a 10-word test with no trials column, a bounded score filed count (as eggprod) and fitted Gaussian as Fox models it; survey year of a repeated cross-section read as a wave. An independent judge (2026-10-24) agreed: the education-only regression fits no wave term, so the fixed-wave rule does not apply.
